name: California

agency.name: California Department of Industrial Relations - Labor Commissioner's Office (DLSE)

rates2027.note: Certified by the Department of Finance on July 31, 2026; DIR news release 2026-66 dated August 13, 2026

tipped.note: Tips cannot be credited toward the minimum wage; tipped workers get the full state (or higher local) minimum wage

minWage.other: Learners (any age) may be paid not less than 85% of the minimum wage, rounded to the nearest nickel, during their first 160 hours of employment in an occupation in which they have no previous similar experience. No separate youth wage: minors get the same minimum wage as adults.

source.quote: Effective January 1, 2026, the minimum wage is $16.90 per hour for all employers, not otherwise covered by a higher minimum wage specific to an industry or a locality.

rates2027Source.quote: Beginning January 1, 2027, California's statewide minimum wage will increase to $17.40 per hour

tippedSource.quote: No. An employer may not use an employee's tips as a credit toward its obligation to pay the minimum wage per hour.

overtime.doubleTime: 2x the regular rate for hours over 12 in a workday and for hours over 8 on the seventh consecutive day of work in a workweek
overtime.seventhDay: 1.5x for the first 8 hours worked on the seventh consecutive day of work in a workweek; 2x after 8 hours that day
overtime.exemptSalaryNote: 2026: twice the state minimum wage for full-time work = $16.90 x 2 x 40 = $1,352/week ($70,304/year), white-collar exemptions. Rises to $72,384/year ($1,392/week) on 2027-01-01.
overtime.note: 1.5x the regular rate for hours over 8 (up to 12) in a workday and over 40 in a workweek.

source.quote: Double the employee's regular rate of pay for all hours worked in excess of 12 hours in any workday and for all hours worked in excess of eight on the seventh consecutive day

exemptSalarySource.quote: As of January 1, 2026, employees in California must earn an annual salary of at least $70,304 to meet this threshold.

sickLeave.accrual: 1 hour for every 30 hours worked (or an up-front grant / alternative accrual)
sickLeave.capNote: Employers may limit use to 40 hours or 5 days per year (whichever is more) and total accrual to 80 hours or 10 days. Up-front policies: 24 hours/3 days by day 120 of employment. Before 2024 the limits were 24 h use / 48 h accrual. Some cities (e.g. Los Angeles, San Francisco, San Diego, Emeryville) have more generous local sick-leave rules.
sickLeave.employerThreshold: all employers; covers employees who work 30+ days for the same employer within a year in California
sickLeave.note: Use may be restricted until the 90th day of employment.

source.quote: the law allows employers to limit an employee's use of paid sick leave to 40 hours or five days during a year ... total accrued paid sick leave to no more than 80 hours or ten days

effectiveSource.quote: An employee who, on or after July 1, 2015, works in California for 30 or more days within a year from the beginning of employment, is entitled to paid sick leave.

familyLeave.name: California Paid Family Leave (PFL), part of State Disability Insurance (SDI), run by the EDD
familyLeave.replacement: About 70-90% of wages (depending on income), based on the highest quarter of the base period, up to the maximum weekly benefit; minimum $50/week
familyLeave.medicalLeave: State Disability Insurance (DI): up to 52 weeks for the worker's own non-work-related illness, injury or pregnancy, same 70-90% formula and $1,765 maximum
familyLeave.stateUnpaidLaw: California Family Rights Act (CFRA): up to 12 workweeks of job-protected leave in a 12-month period; employers with 5 or more employees; employee needs more than 12 months of service and 1,250 hours in the prior 12 months. PFL itself gives no job protection.

source.quote: you may receive benefit payments for up to 8 weeks in a 12-month period. The minimum weekly benefit amount is $50, and the maximum is $1,765 per week.

replacementSource.quote: Your weekly benefit amount (WBA) is about 70-90% (depending on income) of wages you earned 5 to 18 months before your claim start date

benefitsStartSource.quote: Although the legislation was enacted in 2002, PFL benefits officially became available to covered workers on July 1, 2004.

medicalLeaveSource.quote: The most you can receive is 52 weeks of DI benefits, for your own non-work-related illness, injury, or pregnancy.

stateUnpaidLawSource.quote: an employee must have more than 12 months of service with their employer, have worked at least 1,250 hours ... and their employer must have five or more employees

finalPay.fired: immediately at the time of termination, including accrued vacation
finalPay.quit: within 72 hours of quitting; immediately at the time of quitting if the employee gave at least 72 hours' notice
finalPay.quitNotice: 72 hours' notice makes final pay due on the last day
finalPay.ptoNote: Earned vacation vests and cannot be forfeited (no use-it-or-lose-it); all earned, unused vacation must be paid at the final rate of pay at separation. Employers may cap further accrual.

source.quote: An employee who is discharged must be paid all of his or her wages, including accrued vacation, immediately at the time of termination.

ptoSource.quote: upon termination of employment all earned and unused vacation must be paid to the employee at his or her final rate of pay. Labor Code Section 227.3

breaks.meal: 30-minute meal period for work periods over 5 hours (waivable by mutual consent if the day is no more than 6 hours); a second 30-minute meal period for over 10 hours (waivable if no more than 12 hours and the first was not waived)
breaks.rest: Net 10-minute paid rest period for every 4 hours worked or major fraction thereof (more than 2 hours); not required if the day is under 3.5 hours. Missed meal or rest period = one extra hour of pay per day.

source.quote: an employer may not employ an employee for a work period of more than five hours per day without providing the employee with a meal period of not less than thirty minutes

restSource.quote: must authorize and permit a net 10-minute paid rest period for every four hours worked or major fraction thereof

notes.text: Fast-food restaurant employees covered by AB 1228 must be paid at least $20.00 per hour since April 1, 2024 (set by the state Fast Food Council).

source.quote: Starting April 1, 2024, all "fast food restaurant employees" who are covered by the new law must be paid at least $20.00 per hour.

notes.text: Health-care workers at covered facilities have a separate, tiered minimum wage (SB 525) since October 16, 2024. From July 1, 2026: $25 at large health systems (10,000+ FTE), dialysis clinics and large-county facilities; $23 at most other covered facilities; $22 at community/rural clinics; $19.28 at safety-net hospitals and small-county facilities.

source.quote: Hospital or integrated health system with 10,000 or more full-time employees ... 7/1/26 to 12/31/27: $25

notes.text: The statewide minimum wage rises to $17.40 on January 1, 2027, which lifts the exempt-employee salary floor to $72,384 a year.

source.quote: Beginning January 1, 2027, an employee must earn an annual salary of at least $72,384 to meet the salary threshold for exemption.

notes.text: California has daily overtime: time and a half after 8 hours in a day and double time after 12, plus special seventh-consecutive-day rules.

source.quote: Eight hours of labor constitutes a day's work, and employment beyond eight hours in any workday or more than six days in any workweek requires the employee to be compensated for the overtime

uncertain: Long Beach has NO general citywide minimum wage (the state $16.90 applies); it was left out of localMinWages. Only hotel workers have a local rate: $26.50 from 2026-07-01 (longbeach.gov/finance/business-info/compliance/minimum-wage/, which also says the LA County unincorporated rate does not apply in Long Beach).
PFL/DI maximum weekly benefit $1,765: the EDD pages read today show it next to 2026 base-period examples but do not literally say '2026 maximum'. Treated as the 2026 value.
Health-care tiers: the DIR FAQ table read today was last updated June 2025. The July 1, 2026 steps come from that schedule, not from a 2026 notice.

atWill = 'at-will' (Labor Code 2922) and rightToWork = false were not checked against leginfo.legislature.ca.gov because the site returns 403 to automated requests. California has never passed a right-to-work law.
overtime.exemptSalaryWeekly 1352.00 is worked out from DIR's annual figure ($70,304 / 52) and DIR's formula ($16.90 x 2 x 40).

Shape note: extra '*Source' keys (rates2027Source, tippedSource, exemptSalarySource, effectiveSource, replacementSource, benefitsStartSource, medicalLeaveSource, stateUnpaidLawSource, restSource) were added next to the brief's fields so each value has its own official citation, following the brief's ptoSource pattern.

Local entries for San Jose, Mountain View, Sunnyvale, West Hollywood, San Francisco and Emeryville were read in a real browser because those city sites block scripted requests (403/202). Oakland's quote is from its official poster page, reached via redirect.
